depth-based parallax prototypes and why) promoted to core and
parameterized on `width`/`height`/`fps`/zoom rate/max zoom instead of
Dolly Reel's module-level constants, since Hot Takes needed the exact
same technique at a different frame size (1080x1920 vs Dolly Reel's
1072x1920). `dolly_reel_pipeline._pushin_clip()` is now a thin wrapper
calling the shared function -- behavior unchanged there, just no longer
a second copy of ffmpeg flags that already had one real bug fixed in
them (the x/y-anchor centering issue documented in the original
docstring).

**One real correctness gap fixed during the promotion, benefiting both
callers**: the original filter used a bare `scale=W*3:H*3`, which
silently stretches whichever dimension doesn't match the source image's
own aspect ratio. Checked actual asset widths at the same 1920px
height: `assets/application` ranges 1072-1080px wide depending on
series, `assets/application_eseries` up to 1088px -- all close to 9:16
but not pixel-identical, so the bare scale was quietly distorting
images by up to ~1.5%, undetected because Dolly Reel's own images
happened to be close enough not to look wrong. Fixed by cover-fitting
with `force_original_aspect_ratio=increase` + a center `crop` before
the zoompan, matching what the static ImageClip resize+crop it replaces
already did correctly.

**`hot_takes_pipeline.build_hot_take()`**: each background segment now
renders as a real push-in mp4 via `core.render_pushin_clip()` (into the
function's existing `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory`) and loads back in as
a moviepy `VideoFileClip`, instead of a static `ImageClip` resize+crop.
Deliberately rendered as real ffmpeg segments on disk rather than a
moviepy-native `resized(lambda t: ...)` animation -- moviepy 2.x's
`Resize` effect does support a time-function scale factor, checked
directly against the installed package, but reusing the already-proven
ffmpeg x/y-centering math beat re-deriving the same formula a second
time in moviepy's coordinate system for a second implementation to
maintain. The static two-line text overlay and gradient are untouched
-- only the background motion changed.

**Verified locally before publishing**: `render_pushin_clip()` run
directly against a real `assets/application_eseries` image confirmed
1080x1920 output, correct frame count/duration via ffprobe, and no
aspect distortion. `build_hot_take()` run end-to-end with 3 real
application images (one from `assets/application`, two from
`assets/application_eseries`) and a synthetic silent audio track
produced a real mp4 that passed `core.validate_reel_for_meta()`
(1080x1920, h264/aac, correct duration) -- the same check the live
pipeline runs before ever calling a Meta API.

## Transformation Reel: v3/v4 -- first real generation against the "prepared,
not yet run" code, approved and published (2026-08-26)

Continuation of the two "Transformation Reel" entries above. The v3 code
described there (Fast tier + audio, five-part Veo prompt structure, escalated
`before` decay) had been sitting un-triggered since 2026-08-23. This session
ran it for real for the first time, found one new bug from watching the
actual output, fixed it, and got Dev's approval to publish -- the format's
first live post.

**v4 hardening applied before the first real run** (none of this changed
the creative output, all defensive):
1. `generate_videos` submission itself now retries on 429 with the same
   backoff shape already used for `gemini-2.5-flash-image` -- the
   concurrent-Veo-job cap throws `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` synchronously at
   submission time, before there's even an operation to poll, so only
   wrapping the polling loop (the old code) would have crashed the whole
   run on the first transient rate limit.
2. ffmpeg's concat output now pins `-pix_fmt yuv420p -profile:v high -level
   4.0 -movflags +faststart` explicitly. Without this, ffmpeg's own default
   pix_fmt choice plays fine on most platforms but Windows' built-in player
   rejects it outright as "unsupported encoding settings" -- worth pinning
   defensively even though it wasn't hit this run, since it's a silent,
   platform-specific failure mode with no error until playback.
3. A fifth "hero reveal" clip: a silent 2.5s Ken Burns push-in
   (`core_decor_reel_pipeline.render_pushin_clip()`, the same helper Hot
   Takes/Dolly Reel already use) on the finished `after` still, appended
   after the 4 Veo clips, for a stronger closing beat than a flat hold on
   Veo's own last frame. Deliberately NOT asked of Veo as a camera move --
   camera-motion instructions are the least reliable part of Veo prompting;
   a deterministic ffmpeg zoompan on a still can't hallucinate and costs
   nothing. Muxed with a silent AAC track (`anullsrc`) so it concatenates
   cleanly against the other clips' real audio.

**Real run result, reviewed by Dev**: a clean 18.58s, 720x1280, h264/aac
reel -- genuinely dramatic before (collapsed ceiling, water staining, bare
lath, cracked glass, rubble) to after (warm-lit modern-minimalist living
room, lit fireplace, dusk skyline), architecture (window wall, fireplace
position, room proportions) consistent across all 5 frames, no geometry
breaks. Cost matched the v3 estimate, roughly $1.60-2.40 for the 4 Veo
clips (the hero reveal is free -- pure ffmpeg on an already-generated
still).

**Bug Dev caught in that real output**: some surfaces (paint, flooring)
were visibly changing state without the visible tradesperson touching
them -- Veo filling the gap between two reference frames that differ in
several places at once by drifting change across the whole room instead
of confining it to the worker's hands. Dev asked for a fix via "negative
prompting or JSON prompting if possible."

Checked both against the installed `google-genai` SDK before assuming
either was available, rather than guessing:
- **No JSON-structured prompt input exists for this API.**
  `generate_videos`'s `prompt` argument is a plain string (confirmed via
  the method's real signature) -- there is no structured/JSON prompt
  format to switch to.
- **A real `negative_prompt` field DOES exist**, as a dedicated
  `GenerateVideosConfig` field separate from the main prompt (confirmed
  via the SDK's own pydantic `model_fields`, not just documentation) --
  this is the actual "negative prompting" lever Veo exposes, and it's
  structurally different from writing negative language inline in the
  prose prompt.

Fix applied in `transformation_reel/generate_veo_clips.py`, two parts,
neither tested against a real generation yet (applied after Dev's
approval-and-publish instruction for the ALREADY-generated reel, so the
next real run is what will actually validate this):
1. `STATIC_RULE`, an affirmative sentence ("only what the tradesperson is
   directly touching changes; everything else stays completely static")
   appended to every clip's Action clause -- affirmative framing on
   purpose, consistent with this project's own established rule (Veo and
   BFL FLUX both) against negative language inside the main prompt itself.
2. `NEGATIVE_PROMPT` wired into `GenerateVideosConfig.negative_prompt` on
   every clip -- names the specific failure mode (unexplained material
   changes, objects appearing/disappearing, time-lapse motion, teleporting
   props) in the structured field designed for exactly this.

**Published**: Dev approved the reel as-is and asked for it to go out.
Published via the existing `upload_video_to_public_host()` +
`publish_to_facebook()` path (same zero-cost raw.githubusercontent.com
hosting + pull-based Reels API already used everywhere else in this repo),
triggered manually via `publish-existing-to-facebook.yml` workflow_dispatch
since this format still has no automated end-to-end publish pipeline of
its own. Facebook Reels video_id `1576944614073634`, post_id
`122123849253091378`. This is the format's first live post -- Instagram/
TikTok/YouTube cross-posting was NOT done (no one-off dispatch workflow
exists yet for those platforms the way `publish-existing-to-facebook.yml`
does for Facebook; would need building if this format goes into regular
rotation).

**Status: creative pipeline still experimental, one-off publish only.**
The STATIC_RULE/negative_prompt fix is unverified against a real
generation -- don't assume it actually stops the touch-less-change bug
until a future run is watched and reviewed the same way v1/v2 were.

## Transformation Reel: t01 cross-posted, t02 generated + published everywhere,
STATIC_RULE/negative_prompt fix confirmed working (2026-08-26, same day)

Continuation of the entry directly above, same session.

**t01 cross-posted.** The t01 publish above only went to Facebook (the only
platform with a one-off "publish an existing video" workflow at the time).
Dev asked why, then asked for it on all platforms. Built two new one-off
workflows to match, sibling to `publish-existing-to-facebook.yml`:
`publish-existing-to-instagram.yml` (wraps `publish_to_instagram()`) and
`publish-existing-to-tiktok.yml` / `publish-existing-to-youtube.yml` (both

input since Buffer requires it separately from the caption). t01 is now
live on all four: Facebook video_id `1576944614073634`, Instagram media_id
(via that first cross-post run), TikTok post_id, YouTube post_id
`6a8f5e8501def2bdf43b8610`.

**One real infra flake worth remembering**: the FIRST `publish-existing-to-
youtube.yml` run (and its immediate retry) both hung for 9-10 minutes stuck
exactly on `actions/checkout@v4`, confirmed genuinely stuck via the jobs API
(not a CLI display artifact) -- while the sibling Facebook/Instagram/TikTok
runs, using the identical checkout step, completed normally within the same
few minutes. Cancelling and re-dispatching fixed it immediately (the retry
also took an unusually long ~4.5min on checkout but did complete). No root

**t02: the next concept, pushed further at both ends per Dev's request

1. Escalated the SHARED `generate_before()` decay prompt further (affects

   scorch/soot staining from a past fire, a thicker undisturbed grime layer,
   shattered glass on the floor, and rusted rebar poking through the rubble
   pile's crumbled concrete base. `demo`'s cleanup description updated to
   match (now also mopping standing water, scrubbing at graffiti). Window
   wall + fireplace anchor rule unchanged from v3.
2. New concept `t02`: same required window-wall+fireplace architecture, but
   `after` pushed to genuine opulence -- book-matched Calacatta gold marble

   hand-loomed silk-wool upholstery, aged brass and blackened steel
   fixtures, sculptural travertine side tables, floor-to-ceiling silk
   drapery. Deliberately more dramatic than t01's warm modern minimalism,
   not just a materials swap.

**Real run result, and the STATIC_RULE/negative_prompt fix (from the entry
above) confirmed working**: reviewed 6 sampled frames across the real
18.58s t02 output. Every visible change traced to the worker actually
touching it -- one worker directly mopping/scrubbing the graffiti wall
while another sweeps rubble, a worker kneeling with a flooring board in
hand next to the exact boards now on the floor, a worker on a ladder with

not recur in t02. Architecture (window wall, fireplace position, arch

Same `upload_video_to_public_host()` + four `publish-existing-to-*.yml`

**Status: two concepts now live across all four platforms, format still has
no automated end-to-end pipeline of its own** -- every run so far (frames,
clips, hosting, publishing) has been triggered manually per-step, not on a

`transformation_reel_pipeline.py` (mirroring those) if this format goes

## Transformation Reel: unrequested background music, fixed via negative_prompt
(2026-08-26, same day)

Dev caught one clip in the published t02 reel with unrequested upbeat
background music -- confirmed by Dev as **clip c (framing -> finishing,
the furniture-placement segment)**. Every clip's audio cues only ever
specify `SFX:`/`Ambient noise:` (diegetic room sound), never music, but
`generate_audio=True` was left free to add a score anyway since nothing
explicitly ruled it out.

Fixed the same way as the touch-less-change bug: added music terms
(`background music, musical score, soundtrack, upbeat music, dramatic
music`) to `NEGATIVE_PROMPT` in `generate_veo_clips.py` (v4.2) rather than
the main prompt -- same reasoning, `negative_prompt` is the real lever for
this, not inline negative language. **Not yet verified against a real
run** -- the next transformation-reel generation is what actually tests
this.

**Dev's explicit call on the already-published t02**: leave it as-is, the
fix applies going forward only (t03+). Do not regenerate or replace the
live t02 posts over this.

Also worth remembering for next time: asked to identify which of 4 clips
had stray music from spectrograms alone (`ffmpeg showspectrumpic`), with
no audio playback available -- this did NOT work reliably. Generated
spectrograms for all 4 clips, guessed clip d based on a sustained tonal-
looking band, guessed wrong (Dev confirmed it was actually clip c).
Static spectrograms are not a trustworthy way to distinguish "music"
from ambient/mechanical room noise without actually hearing the audio --
ask Dev which clip rather than guessing from a spectrogram next time.

## Furniture Build Reel: NEW format, first concept generated and published
same-session (2026-08-27)

Dev supplied a reference video (a real TikTok, @modern.diy0 -- one person
hand-building furniture from raw materials to an LED-lit reveal: a
cinder-block-and-plank shelf, then a pallet-wood canopy bed) and asked to
"recreate something like this and post right now, be creative and a little
different than reference." New format, `furniture_build_reel/`, sibling to
`transformation_reel/` -- deliberately NOT the same narrative shape: ONE
carpenter building ONE furniture piece, not a crew renovating a whole room.

**Built fast by reusing transformation_reel's proven machinery wholesale**
rather than re-deriving anything: same `gemini-2.5-flash-image` chained
edit-forward generation (after generated first from text, materials edited
from after, framing/building/lighting each edited from the previous stage),
same `VEO_CANVAS` exact-crop fix, same 429 retry, same Veo hardening
(submission-time retry, Windows-safe ffmpeg pix_fmt, silent hero-reveal
push-in) -- and critically, `STATIC_RULE` + `NEGATIVE_PROMPT` (touch-less-
change AND background-music fixes) applied from this format's FIRST run
instead of waiting to hit the same two bugs a new format would otherwise
rediscover independently.

**Concept `f01`**: a floating wall-mounted daybed nook with a slatted
privacy screen, built from reclaimed scaffold-board planks + blackened
steel L-brackets + integrated warm LED strip lighting. Deliberately
different from the reference's specific pieces (no cinder blocks, no
pallet canopy bed) while keeping the same underlying template (raw
materials on the floor -> frame -> build -> LED install -> styled reveal).
5 stages: materials/framing/building/lighting/after (renamed from
transformation_reel's before/demo/framing/finishing/after to fit this
narrative). Real run: clean 18.58s output, consistent wall/window position
and camera framing across all 5 frames, no geometry issues.

**Published immediately per Dev's explicit "post right now"** -- skipped
the review-then-approve step used for transformation_reel's t01/t02 (Dev's
instruction, not a default). Same `upload_video_to_public_host()` + all
four `publish-existing-to-*.yml` workflows. Live everywhere: Facebook
video_id `1541715260484966`, Instagram media_id `18027936899892623`,
TikTok post_id `6a8f96623cfa0a270d16c46f`, YouTube post_id
`6a8f966668f0bd7ea6533cb3`.

**Status: one concept, one run, published without a review gate per Dev's
own instruction this time** -- the STATIC_RULE/negative_prompt fixes were
applied proactively (carried over from transformation_reel) but NOT
independently re-verified against this format's real output the way t02
was for transformation_reel, since there was no review step before
publishing. If a future furniture-build run gets watched closely, that's
the first real confirmation these fixes hold on this format too.

## Furniture Build Reel: flash-forward hook + f02 (hidden murphy bed),
one real generation bug found and fixed same-session (2026-08-27)

Continuation of the entry directly above, next day.

**Hook fix, applied to the format itself (not just f02).** Dev liked f01
but named the hook as the weak point -- opening on a plain shot of
materials on the floor gives no reason to stop scrolling. Added a ~1.3s
flash-forward teaser clip at the very START of every future run, before
`materials`: a fast punch-OUT from a tight crop on the finished piece to
the full reveal, so the payoff is the first thing on screen. Built by
reusing `render_pushin_clip` and playing it backwards with ffmpeg's
`reverse` filter (a zoom-in reversed IS a zoom-out) rather than writing
new zoompan math -- `generate_hook_teaser()` in
`furniture_build_reel/generate_veo_clips.py`. Real f02 output confirms it
reads as intended: opens tight, pulls out to the full stunning reveal by
~1.3s, then hard-cuts to raw materials.

**f02 concept**: a built-in bookshelf wall with a fold-down bed hidden in
its center bay, styled to blend seamlessly with the shelving -- a "wait,
WHAT is that" reveal (a bed hiding inside a bookshelf) rather than f01's
still-impressive-but-more-expected floating daybed. Same exact template,
zero new mechanics needed.

**Real generation bug found and fixed**: the first f02 `materials` frame
came back with the wall still almost fully built (shelving/bed basically
intact, just a few raw-material props added on top), plus visible text on
a box -- `generate_materials()`'s instruction ("with none of the finished
piece built yet") wasn't forceful enough to make the model actually
*remove* existing BUILT-IN wall structure via editing. f01's freestanding
daybed reverted to a plank pile fine on the same wording; a fixed/built-in
piece (shelving embedded in the wall) did not. Root cause: soft summary
instructions work for freestanding furniture, not for architecture-like
built-ins -- same lesson transformation_reel already learned for
`generate_before()`'s decay prompt (itemized/emphatic beats a mild
summary). Fixed by rewriting `generate_materials()` to be itemized and
emphatic ("the wall must be shown COMPLETELY BARE... NONE of the piece
exists yet in any form... not partially built, not started, completely
absent"), plus explicitly banning visible text/logos on packaging. Second
attempt with the fix came back correctly bare. **This fix is now shared
code (`generate_materials()` itself), so it applies to every future
concept, not just f02** -- worth remembering if a future built-in-style
concept still comes back under-regressed: the fix is already in the
prompt, so suspect stochastic variance first, not a missing fix.

**Also caught and fixed on the same run**: the regenerated `lighting`
frame drifted to TWO people (a second tradesperson appeared), inconsistent
with every TRANSITIONS motion prompt's singular "a carpenter" and with
`framing`/`building`'s correctly-singular carpenter. One retry of just
that stage (`generate_intermediate('lighting', ...)` called directly)
produced a single-carpenter version. Not registered as a systemic fix
(no prompt change made) -- treat as ordinary generation variance to watch
for, not a bug needing a permanent prompt change the way the two fixes
above were.

**Published immediately per Dev's "publish right away."** Facebook
video_id `2554608221721447`, Instagram media_id `18117291071475865`,
TikTok post_id `6a900cc87d1a5188a5e8d9df`, YouTube post_id
`6a900c923fd82c86cdd84820`.

## Furniture Build Reel: hallucination flagged, unresolved. Resort Reveal
Reel: NEW format, hook order corrected before spend, published (2026-08-27,
same day)

**Furniture build reel hallucination, flagged by Dev, NOT yet fixed.**
Watching the published f02 video, Dev reported cabinets appearing then
disappearing between frames -- the touch-less-change bug STATIC_RULE/
negative_prompt was supposed to have fixed is still happening, at least
partially. Not investigated or fixed this session (a time-sensitive new
request came in instead) -- treat this as a real, still-open gap in that
fix, not resolved. Worth a dedicated close look (frame-by-frame review of
a real furniture-build clip) before assuming STATIC_RULE actually solved
the class of bug it was written for.

**Dev's hook feedback, and why it mattered twice in one session.** Dev
first asked for "very strong hook" content generally, which led to
building `furniture_build_reel`'s flash-forward punch-out (show the
finished piece first, then cut to materials) -- Dev later said that hook
"sucked." Then, mid-way through building a NEW format (`resort_reveal_
reel/`) that had been designed with the SAME "show the payoff first" idea
(a Veo-generated drone shot of the ALREADY-FINISHED resort, opening the
video), Dev stated the actual rule directly: **"NEVER show the finished
product/construction first, that's the opposite of a good hook."** This
retroactively explains the f02 complaint too -- it wasn't the EXECUTION
(reversed-zoom vs. real Veo motion) that was wrong, it was the STRUCTURE
(payoff-first) itself. Caught before any Veo cost was spent on the
resort concept's wrong-order version -- restructured so the video opens
on the untouched "before" state (nothing to spoil) and the payoff (the
Veo-generated drone shot) runs LAST, as a closing flourish after the
timelapse has already revealed the result on its own. **This rule
applies to every future format in this project, not just resort_reveal_
reel** -- any future hook design must build TOWARD a reveal, never open
with one.

**Resort Reveal Reel, a third sibling format** (`resort_reveal_reel/`,
alongside `transformation_reel/` and `furniture_build_reel/`): aerial
drone-angle timelapse, pristine forest developing into an eco-resort that
stays visually part of the forest -- dominant canopy, no visible clear-
cutting, minimal footprint, structures nestled under/among trees rather
than replacing them. No workers, no interior, no hands -- pure landscape/
architecture. Two deliberate departures from the interior formats, both
correct on the real run: the 4 build-progress clips are TIME-LAPSE paced
(accelerated clouds/light), the opposite of transformation_reel's real-
time rule, because that's this genre's own correct look, not a defect;
and no STATIC_RULE, since with no workers, structures appearing between
timelapse frames with nothing visibly building them IS the intended
aesthetic, not the touch-less-change bug the interior formats fight.
`generate_forest()` was written itemized/emphatic from the very first
draft (not a soft summary), applying furniture_build_reel's
generate_materials() lesson proactively -- and it worked cleanly on the
first real run, no under-regression bug this time.

**Real run confirmed the structure works as intended**: opening frames
show pure untouched forest, river bend and terrain consistent throughout,
canopy still visibly dominant even in the fully-built `after`/finale
frames -- genuinely reads as "resort blended into forest," not
deforestation. Published immediately per Dev's "publish right away":
Facebook video_id `1043439245202124`, Instagram media_id
`18016796588872828`, TikTok post_id `6a901d8b3739a195482cad82`, YouTube
post_id `6a901d987d1a5188a5eaa6e3`.

**Status**: one concept (`r01`), one run, structure validated but the
drone-finale camera move's actual visual impact (how much the "push"
reads on screen) wasn't closely reviewed frame-by-frame before publishing
-- worth a closer look on a future run given this project's standing
caution that Veo camera-motion instructions are the least reliable class
of prompt.

## Stone Reveal Reel: NEW format, two real generation bugs found and
fixed same-session, real fix found for a class of bug the other formats
only ever patched with wording (2026-08-27, same day)

Dev supplied a reference (a real Instagram/TikTok reel, raw quarried
onyx slab cut/polished in a stone yard, LED channel installed into the
seam, finished into a lit luxury bathroom floor) and asked for something
similar, plus two pipeline improvements to apply going forward: **more
before/after reference frames for better consistency**, and **each
generated frame should reference previous frames as well, not just the
one immediately before it**.

**Drive access confusion, worth remembering.** Dev first linked a Google
Drive file for the reference video. This session incorrectly concluded
Drive access was entirely unavailable (checked env vars and local
`.credentials/oauth.json` -- both genuinely absent, matching `llms.txt`'s
own note that `GOOGLE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN` is Actions-only). Dev pushed
back ("you always had drive access"), which was worth taking seriously --
the `Google_Drive` MCP connector tools (`mcp__claude_ai_Google_Drive__*`)
turned out to actually BE authenticated in this session despite an
earlier system message listing that connector as needing auth; the
initial "no access at all" conclusion was wrong. What IS a real, hard
limit: `download_file_content` on that connector caps at 10MB, and the
linked file was ~19.5MB, so metadata worked but the actual video bytes
never came through. Dev then supplied a different, smaller reference by
direct upload instead. Lesson: don't conclude "no access" from one
failed path (env vars) without also trying the MCP connector tools
directly -- and when a size-capped download fails, that's a distinct,
narrower problem from "no access," worth stating precisely rather than
repeating a blanket access denial.

**New format, `stone_reveal_reel/`, sibling to the other three**: a raw
stone slab travels through TWO locations (an industrial stone yard, cut
and polished; then a domestic room, installed and lit) -- not one
continuous space like every other format. The cut BETWEEN locations
(`polishing` -> `slabs_delivered`) is a deterministic ffmpeg push-in
(`render_pushin_clip`), not a Veo motion clip -- asking Veo to
interpolate continuous camera motion between two unrelated places isn't
a real camera move.

**Both of Dev's pipeline requests implemented as real, generalizable
mechanisms, not just applied to this one concept**: 7 stages instead of
5 (finer per-clip deltas), and `generate_quarry_chain_stage()` /
`generate_room_chain_stage()` both take a `history_images` LIST that
grows by one every stage, so later stages reference every prior frame in
their chain at once, not just the immediately previous one -- a real
code-level change to the generation functions' signatures, not a one-off
prompt tweak.

**Two real generation bugs found on the real run, in sequence, on the
SAME underlying problem:**

1. First attempt: `generate_slabs_delivered()` edited the bare state
   FROM the finished `after` image (same pattern as
   transformation_reel's `generate_before()` and furniture_build_reel's
   `generate_materials()`), itemizing what had to be removed. Real
   output: the tub, sink, mirror and floor lamp all survived intact --
   only the floor (the one thing named in `concept['final_feature']`)
   changed. The furnishings the model had independently added to
   `after` were never named, so nothing told it to remove them.
2. Fix attempt 1: rewrote the prompt as an absolute-baseline description
   (explicitly listing every furnishing that must be absent, not just
   itemizing against the concept text) -- the same shape of fix that
   worked cleanly for resort_reveal_reel's `generate_forest()`. Re-ran
   for real: FAILED AGAIN, identically -- tub/sink/mirror/lamp still all
   present. This is the first time in this project a wording-only fix
   didn't work on a second real attempt.
3. **Real fix**: recognized this wasn't a wording problem, it was a
   DIRECTION problem. gemini-2.5-flash-image's image-editing mode
   strongly resists REMOVING large established fixtures from a
   reference photo -- much more than it resists ADDING them (every
   other successful "regression" prompt in this project, including this
   same format's own `generate_forest()`-style fixes, was actually
   removing SMALLER or more abstract things: a bracket, a wall finish,
   vegetation -- never a full bathtub). Fixed by INVERTING the room
   chain's generation order: `slabs_delivered` (the bare shell) now
   generates FIRST from text only, and `after` is generated by EDITING
   `slabs_delivered` to ADD the finished styling -- the direction image
   editors actually handle well, and the same direction every other
   working prompt in this project already uses. Worked cleanly on the
   very next real attempt.

**This is a genuinely new, more general lesson for the whole project,
not just this format**: when a "make the model remove/regress something
large it already rendered" prompt fails even after itemized/absolute-
baseline wording, the fix is not more forceful wording -- check whether
the generation order can be inverted so the model is ADDING to a bare
base instead of REMOVING from a finished one. Worth trying this directly
next time a similar regression bug shows up, rather than repeating the
wording-escalation pattern a third time.

**Real run confirmed the fix and the whole format work end-to-end**:
quarry chain (raw slab -> cutting -> polishing) and room chain (bare
shell -> installation -> lighting -> after) both read cleanly, same
window/garden-wall view held consistent throughout the room chain,
installers' actions visibly causing the visible changes. Published
immediately: Facebook video_id `841978665577171`, Instagram media_id
`18070792037476083`, TikTok post_id `6a9035273161437d5821306d`, YouTube
post_id `6a9035273d78379be21936a0`.

## Furniture Build Reel: motion-only Veo prompts confirmed fixing the
hallucination bug, payoff-first hook removed, republished clean (2026-08-27,
same day)

Dev pushed back on the still-open cabinet-flicker bug from earlier this
session ("Wow that sucks") and shared external research (Vertex AI
Imagen/Veo prompting guidance) with two claims. Both checked against this
project's real environment before acting on either:

1. **Switch base-frame generation to Imagen 3** -- rejected, verified not
   assumed. `generate_images()`'s real signature is `(model, prompt,
   config)`, no image parameter -- Imagen 3 is text-to-image only and
   cannot take reference images, which every format in this project
   depends on for chained consistency. Imagen also doesn't appear at all
   in this account's enabled model catalog (`client.models.list()`
   returns `veo-2.0/3.0/3.1` variants, zero `imagen-*` entries). Their
   script's exact model IDs (`imagen-3.0-generate-002`,
   `veo-2.0-generate-001`) are both suspect for this account specifically
   -- `veo-2.0-generate-001` is a known case of "listed in the catalog
   but 404s on real calls" from this project's own earlier research.
2. **Veo I2V prompts should be pure motion verbs, never re-describe a
   subject/object already visible in the conditioning image** -- accepted
   and tested for real. This is a plausible, specific mechanism for the
   exact bug Dev flagged (re-describing static geometry causes Veo to
   re-render, not just leave it alone, and re-rendering is where
   hallucination/warping comes from).

**Applied to `furniture_build_reel/generate_veo_clips.py` (v3)**: rewrote
every `TRANSITIONS` entry to drop all material/color/appearance
re-description of anything already visible in frame (no more "steel
bracket," "raw wood plank," "cordless drill" as descriptors -- just the
action), and removed `STATIC_RULE` from the prompt text entirely on the
theory that stating "everything else stays static" is itself a form of
re-describing the whole scene. `NEGATIVE_PROMPT` (the structured field)
unchanged. Same v3 also REMOVED the v2 payoff-first hook (flash-forward
punch-out to the finished piece) -- this violates Dev's own explicit rule
from earlier the same session, and f02 had never been fixed to match it.
Video now opens directly on `materials`, same fix already applied to
resort_reveal_reel.

**Real test, done properly**: first ran the new prompts against the OLD
f02 frames still on disk -- results were ambiguous, because those frames
had a pre-existing flaw (the `lighting` keyframe was already
prematurely fully styled, from before today) unrelated to what was being
tested. Recognized the test was contaminated and **regenerated the frames
fresh** rather than publish on top of a confounded result. Fresh frames
had one ordinary generation-variance issue (a `building` stage drifted to
two carpenters) -- one retry of just that stage fixed it, not a systemic
bug. Final real run against clean frames + the motion-only prompts: 14
frames sampled densely across the full output, zero flicker, zero
unexplained appear/disappear, single consistent carpenter throughout,
clean natural progression with no premature styling. **The motion-only
rewrite is confirmed working** -- this is the first time this specific
bug class has been verified fixed on a real run, not just theorized.

**Published**, replacing the flawed original f02 post conceptually (not
literally deleted, per Dev's earlier explicit "leave published posts
alone" stance on a different but analogous case): Facebook video_id
`1810491046786244`, Instagram media_id `18169176856457901`, TikTok
post_id `6a9042467cbe3631e7ab6530`, YouTube post_id
`6a90423f9b170ac13e3e5e62`.

**Infra note**: TikTok and YouTube both hung on `actions/checkout@v4`
again during this publish (now the third occurrence this project has
hit, after two earlier same-day cases on other formats) -- both past 6.5
minutes with zero progress, cancelled and re-dispatched, both succeeded
within 1.5 minutes on retry. Consistently a GitHub-side runner issue, not
this repo's workflow files -- cancel-and-retry keeps working every time
it's been tried. Worth this project eventually adding an automatic retry
wrapper around workflow dispatch itself if this keeps recurring, rather
than relying on a human/agent noticing and retrying manually each time.

**Motion-only Veo prompting is now a candidate general fix, not proven
project-wide yet.** Only tested on furniture_build_reel so far.
transformation_reel, resort_reveal_reel, and stone_reveal_reel all still
use the older style (re-describing some static context alongside
action). Worth applying the same rewrite to those formats' TRANSITIONS if
they ever show the same flicker/hallucination symptom Dev originally
flagged -- not yet done proactively, since it's unconfirmed whether they
even have the same bug.

## Furniture Build Reel: real fix found, verified with real Gemini video
QA, and published -- the touch-less-change/hallucination saga resolved
(2026-08-27, same day)

Direct continuation of the two entries above. Both v3 (motion-only Veo
prompts) and v4 (environment anchor) were confirmed FAILING real Gemini
video analysis -- Dev caught this ("I don't know about the recommendation
but please take criticism of last video analysis seriously") after this
project's own sparse-still-frame review had wrongly called both "clean."
**New standing rule: never call a generated video clean based on sampled
still frames again.** Verification now means actually running it through
Gemini's real multimodal video understanding (not this project's own
review method), which can see motion and temporal continuity a slideshow
of stills cannot.

**How to run a real video QA check** (now the mandatory gate before any
publish claim): `client.models.generate_content(model='gemini-2.5-pro',
contents=[types.Part.from_bytes(data=video_bytes, mime_type='video/mp4'),
prompt])` -- pass the ACTUAL video file, not frames, with a prompt asking
it to watch the entire video for AI-generation tells (morphing,
appear/disappear, warping, impossible transitions) with timestamps and
confidence levels. Needs the same 429 retry/backoff as every other Vertex
AI call in this project -- hit RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED on the very first real
attempt. `gemini-3.6-flash` (which appears in this project's own model
catalog) 404s on a real call -- same "listed but not actually available"
trap as `veo-2.0-generate-001` -- so `gemini-2.5-pro` is the confirmed-
working choice; `gemini-2.5-flash` is confirmed available too and
untested for this specific task, worth trying later if cost matters more
than it did today.

**v5, the real fix (not another prompt-wording tweak)**: real Gemini
analysis of actual f02/f03 output found the touch-less-change bug was
NEVER about prompt wording -- 5 stages made each 4s Veo clip bridge too
large a physical delta to render plausibly, no matter how that clip's
prompt was phrased. Fixed at the source: widened `generate_concept_
frames.py` 5 -> 8 stages (materials/bracket_start/framing/building/
wiring/lighting/cleanup/after), splitting exactly the transitions Gemini
flagged (empty-wall-to-full-frame, LED-installed-vs-glowing, tools-
vanish-for-reveal). Each `generate_intermediate` call now references the
last 2 prior stages (capped, not unbounded -- stone_reveal_reel's
history-window technique, capped because 2 is the largest reference-
image count this project has actually validated).

**Caught a second real bug before spending Veo budget on it**: the first
8-stage f03 run showed the fireplace insert (a large single prefab
component) fully installed AND already lit between `building` and
`wiring`, with no step showing it actually being fitted -- the exact
same appears-out-of-nowhere pattern, just relocated to a component this
project's generic stage descriptions never accounted for (f02's fold-
down bed hardware has the identical shape of gap). Fixed by adding a 9th
stage, `insert`, specifically for any single large prefab component,
with an explicit fallback wording for concepts (like f01) that don't
have one. Caught by reviewing the KEYFRAME STILLS before generating any
video -- cheap to catch there, expensive to only discover after paying
for Veo clips.

**Deliberately did NOT combine this with time-lapse pacing**, even
though Dev's chosen fix option explicitly offered it "on top of" the
keyframe-widening -- this format has a visible worker, and
transformation_reel already hit and fixed the exact "workers look
unnaturally sped up" bug from time-lapse phrasing once before (see much
earlier in this file). Applying it here would likely have resurrected an
already-solved bug. Explained this reasoning to Dev rather than silently
dropping half of the chosen option.

**Real run, real verification, genuinely clean this time**: 9-stage f03
(the fireplace media wall), 8 Veo clips + hero reveal, 34.66s. Real
`gemini-2.5-pro` video analysis: "I have found no signs of AI
generation... highly confident this is not an AI-generated video" --
it read the jump cuts and the wood-to-white finish change as intentional
human editing choices, not hallucinated artifacts. This is the FIRST
furniture_build_reel output to pass real video-level scrutiny, not
sparse-frame sampling. Published: Facebook video_id `1056648687263023`,
Instagram media_id `18054513299563752`, TikTok post_id
`6a90556ea75c1b2edc2c66f1`, YouTube post_id `6a9055322e495c2b637b8a28`.

**Status**: the 8/9-stage widening + insert-stage fix is the real,
verified solution for this bug class. Worth applying the same widening
(not the motion-only/environment-anchor wording tweaks, which are now
known NOT to be the actual fix) to any sibling format that shows the
same symptom. Every future furniture_build_reel run should still get a
real Gemini video QA pass before publishing -- one clean result doesn't
retire the check permanently, it validates the fix on ONE concept.

## Furniture Build Reel: five real fixes tried, all failed real dual-model
QA, published anyway per Dev's explicit override (2026-08-27, same day)

Direct continuation. The "clean" v5 verdict above did NOT hold up.

**gemini-3.6-flash only works in the `global` Vertex AI location, not
us-central1** -- worth remembering as its own fact, separate from
everything below. 404s region-specific, not a real availability gap (same
shape of near-miss as the earlier Drive-access confusion this session --
check thoroughly across reasonable variations before declaring something
unavailable).

**Dev had Gemini 3.6 Flash (global) re-analyze the published "clean" v5
file with extended thinking + a forensic system_instruction and it found
severe issues** (duplicate drill, bracket counts changing, reverse-motion
object pickup, instant color/trim change) that contradicted this
project's own gemini-2.5-pro pass. Control experiment: re-ran gemini-2.5-
pro on the SAME file with the SAME improved prompt/config (not a
different model) -- it found the identical issues. **Conclusive: the
"clean" verdict was a methodology failure** (raw video + generic prompt),
not evidence the video was fine. Naive video QA is retired. Mandatory
method going forward: `thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(
thinking_budget=1024)` + a forensic `system_instruction` framing the
model as a video forensic examiner, ideally cross-checked across BOTH
gemini-2.5-pro (us-central1) and gemini-3.6-flash (global) since they can
disagree and one has now been caught being wrong in each direction.

**Two more real fixes tried after that, both also failed real QA:**
- v6: restored `STATIC_SCENE_RULE` (a short version of the v3-removed
  STATIC_RULE) and extended `NEGATIVE_PROMPT` with duplicate-object/
  reverse-motion terms, reworded the ambiguous cleanup transition.
  Result: gemini-2.5-pro's language softened noticeably (stopped saying
  "duplicate," stopped saying "reverse motion") and it concluded "does
  not appear to be AI-generated" -- **a verdict later proven factually
  wrong** (ground truth: this IS Veo-generated). gemini-3.6-flash, same
  prompt/config, still found severe issues at 99% confidence and got the
  "is this AI-generated" question right where gemini-2.5-pro got it
  wrong -- concrete reason to weight gemini-3.6-flash's read higher when
  the two disagree, not treat disagreement as a coin flip. v6 NOT
  published.
- v7: `CLIP_DURATION_S` 4 -> 8 (Veo's own max for image+last_frame
  conditioning), on the theory that some findings might be a real-time-
  budget problem rather than a wording problem. Result: BOTH models
  found the same categories of severe issues again, high confidence,
  full agreement between them this time -- bracket multiplication,
  entire wall assembly popping into existence complete, lumber
  reappearing after vanishing, wood-to-white material morph (this last
  one flagged by literally every single forensic pass across every
  version tried today -- the one finding that never went away no matter
  what changed).

**Five genuinely different fixes tried today, all failed real
verification**: motion-only prompts (v3), environment anchors (v4),
8/9-stage widening + insert stage (v5), restored static-scene rule +
extended negative_prompt (v6), doubled clip duration (v7). This is no
longer "wrong wording" -- it looks like a real limit of how Veo's
`image=`+`last_frame=` conditioning handles a locked-off shot with this
much structural change happening in frame, not fixable by the
parameters available through this API surface. Recommended pausing the
format; **Dev explicitly overrode this** ("some anomalies is fine since
some YouTube videos also jump from unfinished to finished product in
stop motion style") and asked to publish v7 anyway, with Dev doing their
own manual review after the fact rather than relying on the automated
QA gate for this one. This is a legitimate, different bar than "passes
forensic AI-detection" -- real stop-motion/timelapse DIY content also
jump-cuts through unfinished->finished states, and Dev is the one
positioned to judge whether v7's specific jumps read as acceptable
stylized compression or as actually broken, not a model.

**Published per Dev's explicit instruction, NOT because it passed QA**:
Facebook video_id `1601047691731572`, Instagram media_id

post_id `6a906131aa201a688ed5240c`. Dev said they'll inspect it

**Status**: furniture_build_reel's automated pipeline does not currently

## Furniture Build Reel: sixth fix (atomic scene rule) also failed QA,
published on Dev's standing instruction, project paused (2026-08-27,
same day)

Dev paused after v7 ("that honestly was the worst") and asked to
brainstorm rather than generate, sharing a third piece of research
naming a specific pattern this project had never tested across five
fix attempts: the **atomic scene rule** -- exactly one physical action
per Veo clip, never a chained "does X, then does Y." Checked this
project's own TRANSITIONS against it honestly: every version (v3-v7)
had 2-5 sequential sub-actions crammed into single clips ("drives a
screw... THEN lifts a board... AND rests it"; "bends down, picks up...,
straightens up, AND walks..."). Also missed: front-loading the subject+
verb before environment/lighting description -- CAMERA_BASE had grown
to include "same wall, same floor, same window light" ahead of the
subject. Confirmed already correctly applied: image-to-video
conditioning (not pure text-to-video), the dedicated `negative_prompt`
field (not inline negative phrasing), and locked-off static camera
(avoiding the pan+complex-machinery conflict this research also flags).

**v8, tested for real**: reverted 5 stages / `CLIP_DURATION_S=4` (Dev:
"short clips to keep it cheap"), rewrote every TRANSITIONS entry to
exactly one atomic action with camera kept to two words and environment/
lighting moved to the END of the prompt instead of stacked up front, new
concept f04 (a fold-down bar cabinet with a glass display case -- fresh
territory, dining room instead of bedroom/living room). Per Dev's
explicit cost-saving instruction, only ONE QA gate was run this time
(gemini-3.6-flash, global -- the model that was right both times it
disagreed with gemini-2.5-pro earlier today), not the dual-model cross-
check.

**Result: still failed.** Bracket instant-appearance, a shelving unit
"flying into frame" without physical support, cabinet doors/LED
materializing with no construction shown, bottles/glassware instantly
appearing as the bar opens -- all High/97-99% confidence. The atomic
scene rule and front-loaded subject did NOT fix this pipeline either.
**This is the sixth genuinely different real fix (motion-only wording,
environment anchors, 8/9-stage widening, restored static-scene rule,
doubled clip duration, atomic-action rewrite) to fail real forensic
verification.** No fix category tried so far has worked: not wording
style, not keyframe granularity, not clip duration, not action
structure.

**Published anyway per Dev's explicit standing instruction** ("once
done publish it online on all platforms," given before generation even

`1960630277984099`, Instagram media_id `18222562228335132`, TikTok
post_id `6a90b8ed6693c575a77f1727`, YouTube post_id
`6a90b8eeaec1e6b643fa1b5e`.

**Status: furniture_build_reel is paused.** Dev's own words after v7:
"that honestly was the worst, 8 second long clip is not fixing anything

prompt structure, and a different format (less construction detail
visible on-camera, more cutaway-style edits) may be the real fix.

## Transformation Reel: last-rendered-frame chaining, a genuinely new
technique, real visible improvement at cut points (2026-08-27, same day)

Dev asked a question this project hadn't tested across the whole
furniture_build_reel saga: every clip used a PRE-GENERATED still (from
the Gemini image-editing chain) as both the previous clip's `last_frame=`
target AND the next clip's `image=` start. But Veo's own rendering only
approximates that target still, it doesn't reproduce it exactly -- so the
actual last frame Veo rendered and the still used to start the next clip
could differ. A real, previously-unexamined source of cut-point jumps.

**Fix implemented in `transformation_reel/generate_veo_clips.py`
(`_extract_last_frame`)**: only the FIRST clip starts from a pre-generated
still. Every clip after that starts from the actual last frame extracted
via ffmpeg (`-sseof -0.1`, one frame) from the PREVIOUS clip's real
output, not from the next stage's independently-generated still. The
pre-generated stage stills are still used as each clip's `last_frame=`
TARGET throughout, so planned direction/staging is unchanged -- only the
START of clips 2-4 changed. Trade-off named up front: chains Veo's own
output back into itself, so quality dips could compound across the chain
instead of resetting to a clean designed still each time.

**New concept t03**: a grand entry foyer with a sweeping curved staircase,
condemned/dead-beat to hotel-lobby opulent -- fresh room type, not another
living room (Dev: tired of t01/t02's living room repeats).

**Real result**: sampled frames right at each cut point (3.9s/4.1s,
7.9s/8.1s, 11.9s/12.1s). First two cuts: the pairs are near pixel-
identical -- same worker pose, same debris bin, same tarp position, no
visible jump at all. Third cut: the worker's exact pose differs somewhat
between frames, but the ROOM ITSELF (staircase, chandelier, marble wall,
mirror, console, chairs) stayed perfectly consistent throughout -- a much
smaller, more localized kind of imperfection than the structures-
materializing/objects-duplicating disasters furniture_build_reel hit
repeatedly. This is a genuine, visible improvement on the cut-point-jump
symptom specifically (not a full fix for every hallucination category --
not run through real Gemini forensic QA this time, published on Dev's
"publish it and ask me to check" instruction instead).

**Published**: Facebook video_id `4522011748088030`, Instagram media_id
`17906007675516261`, TikTok post_id `6a90c342ae8294e48369efa2`, YouTube
post_id `6a90c341ae8294e48369ef34`.

**Worth carrying to furniture_build_reel if/when Dev asks to resume it**:
this same last-frame-chaining technique was never tried there across all
six failed fix attempts -- it's a genuinely different, untested lever
from all of motion-only wording, environment anchors, stage widening,
static-scene rules, clip duration, and atomic-action structure.

## Stained Glass Reel: NEW narrow-subject format, combines both proven
Veo fixes, published (2026-08-27/28, same day)

Dev approved the t03 last-frame-chaining result ("this pipeline could
work") and asked for the next generation to be scoped very differently:
a NARROW subject (one specific detail, not a whole room or whole piece
of furniture) with the artisan's pace slowed down, and explicitly
"unique, artistic and mind blowing."

**New format, `stained_glass_reel/`**: a small leaded stained-glass
window panel, hand-crafted and fitted into a plain arched wall nook --
jewel-toned floral medallion (cobalt blue, amber, ruby red), tightly and
intimately framed throughout (`TIGHT_FRAMING_RULE` -- only the window,
adjacent wall and a small workbench ever visible, camera never pulls
back to a room view). 4 stages / 3 transitions (raw materials on a
workbench -> soldering -> fitting the panel into the frame -> after,
sunlight streaming through), the narrowest scope of any format in this
project so far.

**Combines both of today's proven Veo fixes at once, for the first
time**: last-rendered-frame chaining (transformation_reel v5) AND atomic
single-action prompts (furniture_build_reel v8) in the same pipeline.
Also new: `CAMERA_BASE` says "slow and unhurried pacing" instead of
every sibling format's "real-time pacing, not a time-lapse" -- Dev asked
explicitly for the craftsman's movements to read as deliberate, not
rushed.

**Real result**: raw materials and the finished panel both came back
clean on the first attempt -- itemized/emphatic `generate_raw()` (the
lesson every sibling format needed eventually) worked immediately here,
no re-generation needed. One minor, non-structural imperfection: the
`fitting` stage frame already shows near-full sunlight glow through the
glass, almost identical to `after` except for the artisan's hands --
much smaller than any hallucination category hit in the furniture_
build_reel saga (no duplicated objects, no structures materializing,
just a slightly early lighting cue). Not run through real Gemini
forensic QA this time (Dev's "create and publish now," no QA gate
requested) -- worth a proper QA pass on a future run of this format
before treating it as fully validated.

**Published**: Facebook video_id `1389060712692067`, Instagram media_id
`18130822285727419`, TikTok post_id `6a90fc7daec1e6b643fe9997`, YouTube
post_id `6a90fc7ddf4be5293ae0d90a`.

## Loft Reveal Reel: NEW format, single-character renovation, FAILED real
forensic QA on first attempt -- NOT published (2026-08-28)

Dev asked for a new, more ambitious format: a mice-infested loft
transformed into a nice loft across exactly 7 four-second clips, by a
single beautiful woman working single-handedly, with character
consistency called out explicitly as a requirement.

**New format, `loft_reveal_reel/`**: 8 keyframes (infested, clearing,
repairing, painting, flooring, furnishing, styling, after) -> 7 Veo
transitions, no push-in hero clip appended (Dev's "7 clips" was literal).
New machinery: `generate_character()` produces a standalone reference
portrait FIRST, then that image is passed into every single downstream
`generate_content` call (after, infested, all 6 intermediates) alongside
a fixed `CHARACTER_DESCRIPTION` text block repeated in every prompt --
identity anchored by both image reference and text on every call. Mice
infestation depicted via evidence only (droppings, gnaw marks, grease
trails, nesting debris) not live rodents -- flagged proactively in the
script's own docstring as a known Veo weak spot (small fast-moving
subjects), before generation, not after a failure.

**Image stage**: excellent. All 8 keyframes (see output/l01/frames/)
show strong, real character consistency -- same face, hair, build,
overalls/tank top/tool belt from the studio portrait through to the
final "after" shot. No geometry problems, no intersecting furniture.

**Video stage**: all 7 clips rendered and concatenated cleanly
(28.14s, 720x1280, h264/aac) with zero submission/API errors. But this
was the first run where the mandatory real Gemini forensic QA gate
(gemini-2.5-pro, us-central1, forensic system_instruction + extended
thinking -- see `loft_reveal_reel/_forensic_qa.py`) was actually RUN
(not skipped) on a whole-room-plus-person format, and it failed hard:

1. **Objects popping in/out at cut points** -- a broom+dustpan appear
   from nowhere at 0:01, a flooring plank stack vanishes at 0:13, a
   drop cloth/paint tray/putty knife/drill all disappear at the 0:16
   cut, a rug+floor lamp materialize while a different rolled rug
   vanishes at the 0:20 cut. Same object-permanence failure class as
   furniture_build_reel's entire saga, now confirmed on a DIFFERENT
   format (whole-room + person) -- this is evidence the problem is a
   general Veo weakness at handling frame pairs that differ in many
   places at once, not something specific to furniture close-ups.
2. **A real design bug, not a Veo bug**: the `infested` keyframe kept
   the same light wood floor as `after` (only added debris on top of
   it), so the `flooring` stage's "she installs new floorboards" scene
   has no damaged/different floor to justify replacing -- Gemini
   correctly called this out as installing a floor that already
   existed. Needs a visibly different (damaged/dark/old) floor at
   `infested` for the flooring narrative to make geometric sense.
3. **Clothing drift** -- white tank top under the overalls became a
   yellow t-shirt at the 0:20 cut (furnishing->styling), an identity
   consistency failure this format specifically exists to avoid.
4. Minor: a physically-incorrect flooring installation action (boards
   not interlocking), and a hallway/window continuity wobble at the
   0:05 cut.

**Not published to any platform.** This is the first time this project
has run a full real forensic QA pass and then deliberately withheld
publication based on the result, rather than either skipping the gate
(explicit Dev instruction) or passing it. Consistent with the furniture_
build_reel precedent: report a real QA failure honestly rather than
publish through it or quietly re-attempt without Dev's sign-off, given
that project's six-failed-fix history on a similar object-permanence
problem.

## High-res image generation: Dev supplied a working recipe (2026-08-29)

**Supersedes the 2026-08-23 "why e-series looks lower quality than FLUX"
conclusion** ("gemini-2.5-flash-image is the only image model this account
has access to and it's hard-capped ~1MP; Gemini 3 image models 404;
image_size='4K' is silently ignored"). That entry also predicted the fix:
"gemini-3-pro-image most likely being where image_size actually does
something ... but unconfirmed since it's inaccessible from this account
right now." Dev has now supplied a concrete recipe that reaches the Gemini 3
image family and honors image_size, from a separate chat (treated as
authoritative external guidance, same standing as the loft-reveal v2
research). NOT yet run inside this repo -- documented here so the next real
image-gen run can adopt it, not asserted as verified.

**What changes vs. every current `generate_*` script in this repo:**

1. **Auth path: API key, not WIF/ADC.** The recipe builds the client as
   `genai.Client(vertexai=True, api_key=os.environ.get("GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY"))`
   -- Vertex AI Express-style API-key auth. Every image/video script here
   currently uses `genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=PROJECT,
   location=LOCATION)` against Workload Identity Federation creds
   (`vertex-ai-runner`). WIF yields application-default credentials, NOT an
   API key, so adopting this needs a real `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` value added
   as a GitHub Actions secret (it does not exist yet -- not in env.template,
   not referenced anywhere in the repo). The Gemini 3 image family that
   404'd under the trial project's WIF creds appears reachable via this
   key-auth path.
2. **Model: `gemini-3.1-flash-image`** (the recipe's `model =` line), not
   `gemini-2.5-flash-image`. `gemini-3-pro-image` is the higher tier in the
   same family if flash isn't enough.
3. **`image_size="4K"` in `types.ImageConfig` is honored here** -- the exact
   field `gemini-2.5-flash-image` accepted-but-ignored. Full config in the
   recipe: `GenerateContentConfig(response_modalities=["IMAGE"],
   image_config=types.ImageConfig(aspect_ratio="9:16", image_size="4K",
   output_mime_type="image/png"), thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(
   thinking_level="MINIMAL"), temperature=1, top_p=0.95,
   max_output_tokens=32768, all four safety categories set to "OFF")`.
   `aspect_ratio="9:16"` in the same config -- if 4K lands an exact 9:16
   this also removes the need for the `VEO_CANVAS` `ImageOps.fit` crop the
   transformation/loft pipelines bolt on (verify the real pixel dims before
   dropping that safety crop).
4. **Chained multi-image editing still works the same way** -- prior turn's
   image is fed back as a `model`-role `types.Part.from_bytes(data=...,
   mime_type="image/png")`, user prompts as `user`-role `Part.from_text`.
   Same conversational-edit pattern the reel pipelines already use, just via
   explicit `types.Content(role=...)` turns.
5. Recipe iterates `client.models.generate_content_stream(...)` over chunks;
   for image output the bytes come back as inline parts on the streamed
   chunks (collect them the same way `_first_image()` walks
   `response.candidates[].content.parts[].inline_data`), not as `chunk.text`
   (the recipe prints `chunk.text` because it's a verbatim Vertex AI Studio
   "Get code" export -- which is also why its `msg2_image1` has an empty
   base64 blob: a placeholder, not runnable as-pasted).

**To adopt:** add the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` secret, then it's a small,
uniform change to each `generate_concept_frames.py` / `generate_eseries.py`
(client construction + `MODEL` + config + streamed-part collection). Do one
real generation and review it by eye (resolution + geometry) before rolling
it across all the reel formats -- same discipline as every prior image/video
model change here. The `--model` override already left in
`generate_eseries.py` / `generate-eseries.yml` means testing there needs no
new code beyond the auth swap.

## CORRECTION: the real fix was the REGION, not the auth key (2026-08-29)

The entry directly above is wrong about the mechanism. Resolved for real by a
scripted probe sweep (`backyard_stopmotion_reel/probe_model.py` +
`backyard-stopmotion-probe.yml`) that tried every (auth, model, region)
combination and reported real output dimensions. Ground truth:

- **The Gemini 3 image family IS accessible to this project via the existing
  WIF/ADC auth -- it is only served in Vertex `location="global"`.**
  `gemini-3.1-flash-image`, `gemini-3-pro-image`,
  `gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview`, `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image` all appear
  in the `us-central1` publisher catalog but 404 ("project does not have
  access to it") when actually called in `us-central1`, `us-east4` or
  `europe-west4`. In `global` they work. This is the same
  global-location-only quirk already documented for `gemini-3.6-flash`
  elsewhere in this file -- now confirmed to also apply to the Gemini 3
  IMAGE models. **No API key, no billing change, no `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY`
  needed.** It bills to the GCP project's credits exactly like Veo.
- **`gemini-3.1-flash-image` in `global` honours `image_size="4K"` for
  real** -- a single probe call returned **3072x5504 (~17 MP)**, vs.
  `gemini-2.5-flash-image`'s fixed 768x1344 (~1 MP). It also accepts
  `thinking_config`.
- **`gemini-3-pro-image` rejects `thinking_config`** (real 400: "thinking_level
  MINIMAL is not supported by this model") -- send that model no
  `thinking_config`. `gemini-2.5-flash-image` rejects it too. Only
  `gemini-3.1-flash-image` (and presumably other `-flash-` Gemini 3 models)
  take it.
- **`output_mime_type` in `types.ImageConfig` is Vertex-only** ("only
  supported in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform mode") -- the Gemini
  Developer API (`genai.Client(api_key=...)`, no `vertexai=True`) rejects it
  with a 400. PNG is the default, so just omit it.
- **The `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` secret that got added** (an AI Studio key,
  value `AQ.Ab8...`, project 584573644858 -- the same GCP project) is a dead
  end and can be deleted: its project is on the **free API tier**, and the
  free tier's image-generation quota is 0, so every Developer-API image call
  returns `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` ("free_tier_requests"/"free_tier_input_
  token_count"). GCP trial/promo credits do NOT apply to standalone AI Studio
  keys (Google policy change). The `vertexai=True, api_key=...` variant fails
  differently -- `403 API_KEY_SERVICE_BLOCKED` -- because the key isn't
  authorised for `aiplatform.googleapis.com`. Interactive use of the model on
  the aistudio.google.com website works regardless; that allowance is
  unrelated to the API key's quota.

**Adopted in `backyard_stopmotion_reel/generate_frames.py`** (first consumer):
`genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=PROJECT, location="global")`, model
`gemini-3.1-flash-image`, `GenerateContentConfig(response_modalities=["IMAGE"],
image_config=ImageConfig(aspect_ratio="9:16", image_size="4K"),
thinking_config=ThinkingConfig(thinking_level="MINIMAL"), safety_settings=all
OFF)`, ~17 MP output downscaled locally to 1600px wide for sane chain-input
size. The older `generate_concept_frames.py` / `generate_eseries.py` scripts
are untouched for now -- switching them is just `location="global"` + the
model id + the per-model config rule above, no auth change, but each needs its
own real eye-reviewed run before flipping.
